sections.html:
Williston sits in the northwest corner of North Dakota where U.S. Highways 2 and 85 cross, near the meeting of the Yellowstone and Missouri rivers at the head of Lake Sakakawea. The Montana border is 18 miles away. The city covers about 25.9 square miles and dates to 1887.

The population roughly doubled in a decade, from 14,716 in 2010 to 29,160 in 2020, with an estimate of 29,522 for July 1, 2025. The surge came with oil and gas drilling in the Bakken shale. Homes here were built or bought in a short span, and buyers compare them closely, so condition and paperwork often decide a sale.

Winter runs the maintenance calendar. Snowfall averages 48.2 inches a season, and the January mean temperature is 11.5 degrees Fahrenheit. Inspectors and buyers focus on furnaces, insulation, roofs that hold snow and any plumbing exposed to freezing.

The city limits camper vehicles and other nonpermanent structures as permanent housing, and the rules reach owners as well as occupants. If workers have been parking RVs on a lot you own, sort that out before you sell.

Chapter 5.5 of the city code bars permanent habitation in a camper vehicle in residential, commercial and industrial zones. A violation brings a written warning to the camper's owner or, if that person can't be found, to the owner of the parcel. Outside the construction-site guidelines, the ordinance makes a violation a class B misdemeanor with a fine of $500 per day per camper vehicle.

  • Construction sites may house workers in RVs, up to 10 units, under a monthly permit that costs $200.
  • RVs must be gone before the city will issue a certificate of occupancy.
  • Residents and visitors may use a camper on developed property for seven days without a permit, and no more than 28 days in a calendar year.

The zoning ordinance defines temporary workforce housing separately, and the list of amendments shows moratoria on processing workforce housing applications and on tent structures. Read the code on the city's code site, or ask Planning and Zoning how your parcel is classified.

A deed can split the minerals from the surface, and North Dakota law sets default readings. Under N.D.C.C. 47-10-25, a surface deed signed on or after July 1, 1983 that reserves any minerals is treated as reserving every mineral of any kind unless some are excluded by name. Gravel, clay and scoria go with the surface unless the deed reserves them by name.

Section 47-10-24 works the other way for conveyances of mineral rights, reading them to convey all minerals except those specifically excluded by name. Wording decides everything here, so find your vesting deed and any earlier reservations before you agree on a price. A title company or attorney can confirm what you own, and that answer should be in hand before you list so buyers aren't left guessing. Both sections appear in the legislature's Title 47 chapter 10.

Williams County bills and collects the tax on Williston homes under the state formula. Assessed value is half of market value, and a residential property's taxable value is 4.5 percent of true and full value. The total mills of the bodies taxing your parcel are applied to that.

If no statement has reached you by December 31, contact the Treasurer. The county's iTax system lets you search parcel valuations and current bills. More is on the county's property information page.

Williston's zoning ordinance requires a permit from the City Building Official before any development in a special flood hazard area. If your property sits near water or low ground, ask the city whether it's mapped, and keep permit history for improvements.

Gather the paperwork for each improvement you made, including who did the work and when. Buyers and their lenders often ask for it, and a tidy folder shortens the inspection period.

Owners downtown must also apply to the Design Review Board before a building permit, and the ordinance limits accessory buildings and signs by zoning district. Since the city grew so fast, check that additions, garages and finished basements were permitted. Unpermitted work is easier to resolve before a listing than during an inspection period.

A North Dakota seller of a residential dwelling with up to four units gives the buyer a written disclosure of material facts before final acceptance (N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1). Foreclosure sales, estate fiduciary sales and some transfers to family are excepted. Section 47-10-02.2 requires a separate written radon disclosure.

Williston owners can list, sell on their own, or take a cash purchase by a buyer who accepts the house as-is. Cash is worth comparing when the house was a rental or crew house, has deferred maintenance, or is an inherited property you don't want to manage. We don't quote prices here, but Cash Home Buyers can review a Williston address and explain how an offer works. Declining costs you nothing.

In a cash sale the title company pays taxes and any liens from your proceeds, so the number you receive is the net. There are no showings, and no lender appraisal delays the date.

sections.h2: Before you sell: a short checklist
sections.html:
• Look up your parcel on the county's iTax system and note the current bill.
  • Decide whether to take the 5 percent discount by paying in full on or before February 15, or the penalty-free March 1 date.
  • Remove any RVs and confirm no camper violations are open on the parcel.
  • Find your vesting deed and read the mineral reservations.
  • Gather permits for additions, garages and finished basements, and check the flood map for your address.

If a crew house or rental is part of the picture, add the lease details and any city warning letters to the pile. A buyer who purchases as-is still wants to know what they're taking on, and an honest list from you makes an as-is price easier to agree on.

Having these answers ready lets a buyer or title company move quickly and keeps surprises out of the inspection period.

faqs.q: How many people live in Williston, ND?
faqs.a: The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 29,522 residents. The April 2020 census count was 29,160 and the 2010 count was 14,716.

faqs.q: Can workers live in RVs on my Williston lot?
faqs.a: Only in limited cases. The camper ordinance bars permanent habitation in campers in most zones, lets construction-site RVs operate under a $200 monthly permit, and fines violations $500 per day per camper. Confirm your parcel's zoning with the city.

faqs.q: Do I keep the minerals when I sell a Williston house?
faqs.a: It depends on the deed. A surface deed that reserves minerals is read as reserving all of them unless some are excluded by name, and gravel, clay and scoria pass with the surface unless reserved. Have a title professional read your deed.

faqs.q: When are Williams County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills are due the January 1 after the year of assessment, and March 1 is the last penalty-free day. Paying in full by February 15 earns a 5 percent discount.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Williston house that has deferred maintenance?
faqs.a: Yes. You still give the buyer the written disclosure North Dakota requires, and a buyer who purchases as-is decides whether to take the house in its present condition.
